items.name: Sandthrone toll-book
items.description: The toll-master's book, bound in greasy hide and thick with thumbprints.

items.name: Seeker's warrant
items.description: Folded orders under a Seeker's seal. The seal is already broken.

items.name: Rockhide
items.description: Thick, stone-grey boar hide that barely bends.

items.name: Salt-Mender letters
items.description: Folded papers in a waxed pouch, written in a cipher of salt-marks.

items.name: Soot-black journal
items.description: The waystation keeper's journal, wrapped in oilcloth.

items.name: Pib's list of names
items.description: A page in big, careful letters, folded round a chip of grey stone. Five names, and a space.

items.name: Grey-tipped bristle
items.description: A rockhide's bristle, pulled with the root. The tip is grey, smooth and cold; the root is not.

items.name: Old Scree-Tusk's grey hide
items.description: Grey right through and smooth as river stone. It weighs next to nothing, and it is never warm.

documents.title: The Cairn-Book
documents.text:
An oilcloth book from the top of the pilgrims' cairn above the tarn. A line for every crossing, in a dozen careful hands: the Silent Pilgrims write what they will not say.

South, in spring. Jars empty. The pass held its note.
North, at harvest. Three jars full. One cracked on the scree; what was in it is the mountain's now.
South. The new masters at the gate took a sovereign each. We paid. Silence is not the same as quarrel.
North. Snow in summer. The tarn sang once after dark, very clear.
South. One of us, alone, carrying the others' jars. Do not ask.
North. Nothing heard at the scarp's foot. Nothing at all. Write it down anyway.

The last line is in a hand unlike the others: WHO READS THIS, ADD YOURS. Below it the page is empty.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims, their silence and their echo-jars are CANON (world_bible.md); the cairn, its book and its lines are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Toll-Runner's Reckoning
documents.text:
A greasy page from a runner's satchel, figures down one side and a plan down the other:

Owed at the gate if I go through: one in ten of the salt, a sovereign for me and a sovereign for the mule.
Owed if I go round: nothing.

The way round: up past the crag, over the shoulder where the old slide came down, along the scree and back to the road below the gate. Two hours. Goats do it.

The Sandthrone don't watch the slide. Nothing comes down it twice, they say.

The last figure is a sum with a line drawn under it, and nothing written after the line.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the runner and his reckoning. The Sandthrone toll on the Peaks is CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md).

documents.title: The Toll-Book
documents.text:
SANDTHRONE TOLL - HIGH GATE
kept by the toll-master's hand

14th day. Salt-carter, two mules. 3 sovereigns. Paid.
15th day. Pilgrims, six, for the south. 1 sovereign each. Four paid; two held till paid.
17th day. Oakhaven run, by Khaven. Two, small. Received from our riders.
    Handed on at the gate to the Concord escort: four horse, one closed cart. Road to Argentis.
    TOLL: none. By Seeker's warrant. Captain has the paper.
18th day. Iron, four carts, north road. 12 sovereigns. Paid.
19th day. Goatherd. Took two goats.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the toll-book and its entries. Sandthrone tolls in the Peaks are CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md).

documents.title: Under a Seeker's Seal
documents.text:
BY WARRANT OF THE HIGH COUNCIL
Seeker's Office, to the Sandthrone captain of the Peaks toll

The bearer's escort passes the gate without toll or search, with its cargo: resonance candidates, two, collected at Oakhaven by the Investigation Bureau. They are to reach Argentis sound. Damage to the cargo will come out of your Company's fee.

A third candidate (the miller's boy) follows by the next wagon. Pass it likewise.

On the third passing, send word down the east road to the Bureau's man at Oakhaven. The seed already lies in the village water. It is to be woken then, and not before.

- the Seeker's mark -
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Seekers, the Investigation Bureau and the Void-Seed in Oakhaven's water are canon (book1 ch.4); the warrant and its wording are GAME-ONLY. Where the children are taken is left open.

documents.title: The Waystation Keeper's Last Page
documents.text:
Third day of the new masters on the gate. They want a toll off the waystation now. A toll on bread.

Fifth day. Paid it. Paid it again when a different one came asking.

Sixth day. Torches on the lower road. I've sent the pilgrims out by the goat path with what bread there was, and I'm putting this in the hearth where I put everything. If you're reading it, lay a stone for me on the cairn below the gate.

Grenna Holt, keeper.

documents.title: Six on the Goat Path
documents.text:
Pencilled very small on the back of a pilgrim's token:

Six of us out of the waystation by the goat path, the night the torches came up the road. Grenna gave us the bread and would not come. She said someone had to keep the hearth lit, or they'd know.
Cold here. No fire after dark; they would see it from the gate.
We go on over the top at first light, south, for the Archive.
If you find this, Grenna: we made it this far.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the pilgrims and their camp. The Archive of Silence in the south is CANON (world_bible.md).

documents.title: To Ysolde, by Any Caravan
documents.text:
To Ysolde at the Dry Wells, in the south, by any caravan:

Sister, the pay is good, as they promised, and the cold is worse than they said. Snow in the middle of summer. They have us stopping carts on a mountain road and taking what we like and calling it toll, and most of the lads like it well enough.
I don't. Last week we passed two little ones through the gate in a closed cart, under a paper with a seal I'm not to speak of. No toll. They didn't cry. That was the worst of it.
When I've enough I'm coming home. Keep the goats.
Your brother, Tomas
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the letter, Tomas and Ysolde. The Sandthrone is a CANON mercenary company; its toll in the Peaks is CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md).

documents.title: What the Jar Remembers
documents.text:
Unstopped, the jar gives back a voice, very far off, in no tongue you know, and yet you understand it:

'...and the river said its own name, and every stone in it answered, and that was the first song. We did not make it. We only learned to hum along. Remember that, when they tell you the Weave is theirs to spend...'

Then only the wind in the jar, and your own breath.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: echo-jars, the Silent Pilgrims and the Original Song are CANON (world_bible.md); the words in this jar are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Foreman's Notice
documents.text:
NOTICE. The Umbra working is closed by the foreman's order.

The deep level has gone bad. The stone down there is grey and smooth and does not ring under the pick. It makes no sound at all. Pell put his pick into it and drew it back without its point: not broken off, gone, clean, as if it had never had one.

We have walled the mouth with good mortar. Do not open it, for any price. The grey has got into the roots of the mountain.

- Bram Tolley, foreman
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: old mining tunnels under the Shattered Peaks (book2 ch.19) and the void slowly eating the Peaks' stone (world_bible.md) are CANON; the working, its foreman and this notice are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: What the Grey Stone Remembered
documents.text:
Written large and careful, in a goblin's hand not used to these letters:

HEARD IN THE GREY STONE OFF THE WALKERS BY THE OLD ADIT
by Pib of the Warrens, as near as the stone said it

PELL. Remembers the sound his pick did not make.
OSWY DUNN. Remembers bread burnt on the bottom, and being told off for it.
GIL and GARRET MABE, brothers, in the one stone. They remember each other.
WAT CORLEY. Remembers somebody singing in the dark to keep the others brave. He thinks it was him.
The fifth stone had forgotten already. I am sorry. I listened a long time.

Below it, in Maddoc Vire's hand: Entered in the book of the Rest. Went up the road. Did not come down.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the miners and their names. The Hollow Men (book1 ch.4) and the goblins as the old record-keepers (world_bible.md) are CANON.

documents.title: Where the Pass Still Sings
documents.text:
Copied fair from Brother Cael's slate, in a small, upright hand:

The Cold Tarn, north shore, after dark. Heard: one note, clear, like a glass struck once. The water remembers.
The foot of the Umbra scarp. Heard: the mountain's own note, low and slow. Old. Whole.
The Broken Post, on the east road. Heard: nothing. The wind out of the east carries no note at all, not even its own.

It is coming from the east. We knew. Now it is written.

To be carried south to the Archive by whichever of us goes over next.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims, the Original Song and the Archive of Silence are CANON (world_bible.md); Brother Cael's notes are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Pilgrims' Crossings
documents.text:
Pressed between two flat stones in the cairn at the spur's end, a page in the careful hand of the Silent Pilgrims:

One stone for every crossing. We have crossed since the Archive was young: south to north in spring with the echo-jars empty, north to south in autumn with them full. The pass holds the song still. At the tarn, the Earth note. At the shrine, the Spirit. At the spur's end, where the wind drops, the Silence, which is not nothing. It is the sound of the mountain holding.

The mountain is being eaten from the east. We hear it in the Silence now, a grain at a time. Elder Orym says a thing that is eaten slowly can be sung whole again, if one knows the song. We do not know the song. We know where it was.

The Company has put a gate on the road and calls it a toll. We pay in stones, as we always have. They have not yet learned to count stones.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims, the Archive of Silence, Elder Orym, the Original Song's three notes and the void eating the Peaks' stone are CANON (world_bible.md, book3 ch.5); the cairn, the crossings and the page are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: What the Watchers Count
documents.text:
A leaf from a Salt-Mender's notebook, weighted with a stone on the ledge above the east road:

Fourth night on the ledge. The pale shapes do not watch the road; they watch what comes up it. I have tested this. A mule: no interest. A pilgrim: one of them turned. Me: all of them.

They are not sentries. A sentry stops you. These let you pass and make a mark. I believe they are auditors, in the old sense: they come to see whether the account is true. Whose account, I cannot say. The Council's, I would guess, since the Council has been drawing on something for three hundred years and has never once shown the ledger.

If they are counting us toward a sum, there will be a day the sum is reached. I would like very much to know the number. I would like more to be somewhere else on that day.  - L. T.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Pale Things as cosmic auditors and the Council's hidden cost are CANON (world_bible.md); Lisle Tamber, the Salt-Menders' scholar, and her notebook are GAME-ONLY.

quests.title: The Toll-Book
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Sandthrone tolls in the Shattered Peaks are CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md); the toll-book and the handover to a Concord escort are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Fight through the Sandthrone toll-guards at the gate and take the toll-book from the strongbox by the toll-house.
quests.offer:
"Paid before they got here. Paid by whom?" Maddoc taps the page. "The Sandthrone write everything in their toll-book: who passed, what they paid, who paid it for them. They're proud of that book. They keep it in a strongbox by the toll-house, behind the gate."

"I can't ask pilgrims to fight for it. You aren't a pilgrim."
quests.complete: "Here." Maddoc's finger stops on the page. "'Two, small. Oakhaven run. Handed on at the gate to the Concord escort. Road to Argentis. No toll: by Seeker's warrant.'" He closes the book gently, as if it might wake. "A Seeker's warrant. That's the Council's own hand."

steps.text: Break the toll-guards at the gate.
Take the toll-book from the strongbox by the toll-house.

objectives.say: The strongbox lid gives with a crack. Coin, a knife, and a thick book bound in greasy hide.

steps.text: Bring the toll-book to Maddoc Vire.

objectives.say: "Let me see it." He wets a finger and turns the pages back a fortnight.

quests.title: Under a Seeker's Seal
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Seekers and the Level 4 Void-Seed in Oakhaven's water are canon (book1 ch.4); the warrant, the captain and the Void-Seed's timing are GAME-ONLY. The children's fate is left open.
quests.summary: Take the Seeker's warrant from the Sandthrone captain in his eyrie above the toll gate, then show it to Tarsk the Ash-Walker.
quests.offer:
"'Captain has the paper.'" Maddoc says it twice. "The captain keeps the high camp above the gate, where he can watch the whole road. He's no toll-guard. He fights like the Peaks belong to him."

"If there's a warrant, it'll say where the children went, and why. Bring it back, and show it to Tarsk. He sits by my door and says nothing, but he reads, and he knows things about the grey I'd rather not."
quests.complete: "The children are gone up the road to Argentis. I know nothing that goes up that road and comes back." Tarsk taps the last lines of the warrant. "But this I know. A seed in your village water, waiting for a word. My people have seen what a seed does when it wakes."

steps.text: Take the Seeker's warrant from the Sandthrone captain above the toll gate.

objectives.say: Inside the captain's coat, in an oilcloth wrap: folded orders under a Seeker's seal, already broken.

steps.text: Show the warrant to Tarsk, the Ash-Walker scout at the rest.

objectives.say: Tarsk reads it once. Then he reads the last lines again, and lays his hand flat on the paper as if to hold something down.

quests.title: Salt of the First Sea
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Mother Vane the Salt-Speaker, Salt of the First Sea and the enclave in the caves of the Eastern Ridge are canon (book1 ch.20); that salt can bind a Void-Seed is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Follow the toll road down to the Ashland Rim and ask Mother Vane, the Ash-Walkers' Salt-Speaker, for salt to bind the seed in Oakhaven's well.
quests.offer:
"Salt binds what the grey unmakes. Not your kitchen salt. Salt of the First Sea, the old salt, spoken over by one who knows its words." Tarsk stands for the first time since you came. "Mother Vane knows them. Our enclave is in the caves of the Eastern Ridge, down the toll road where the land turns to ash."

"She won't give it to you. Salt is not given. But she may let you earn it."
quests.complete: Mother Vane hears you out without a word, turning a pinch of white salt between finger and thumb. "Aye. Salt of the First Sea will bind a seed. Bind it, mind. Not unmake it." She lets the salt fall. "And it's not given. It's earned."

steps.text: Follow the toll road down to the Ashland Rim.

objectives.text: Go down to the Ashland Rim
objectives.say: The toll road drops out of the Peaks onto a plain of grey ash. Nothing grows. Far to the east a ridge of dark rock stands against a bruised sky, and beyond it, the grey static of the Wasting.

steps.text: Find Mother Vane at the Ash-Walker enclave on the Eastern Ridge.

objectives.say: "Tarsk sent you. He sends me strays and expects me to feed them." Her eyes are blue and entirely too sharp. "A seed in a well. Hm. Sit down. Tell me all of it."

quests.title: Stones for the Lost
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (a burial custom of the pass)
quests.summary: Lay a stone on each of the three pilgrims' cairns along the toll road.
quests.offer:
"Every pilgrim who dies on this road gets a cairn, and every pilgrim who passes lays a stone on it. That's the custom." He looks at the empty benches. "Not many pass now. The cairns go bare, and the old folk say a bare cairn lets the dead wander."

"There are three along the road: one below, on the way up from Khaven, and two past the gate. A stone on each. Say their names if you know them. I don't, anymore."
quests.complete: "Good." Maddoc opens his book to a page of names and runs his thumb down it. "They'll rest a while longer."

steps.text: Lay a stone on each pilgrim cairn along the toll road.

quests.title: Wolves on the Mule Track
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Cull six mountain wolves in the pines on the western slope.
quests.offer: "I've three mules left, and the wolves in the west pines have learned the sound of their bells." Yara slaps dust from her trader's coat. "Six of them. Enough that the rest learn a new sound."
quests.complete: "My mules will sleep tonight. So will I." She counts coin onto the stall without haggling, which for Yara is a kind of thanks.

steps.text: Cull the mountain wolves in the west pines.

quests.title: Rockhide
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Bring Yara five rockhides from the boars in the wallow on the southern slopes.
quests.offer: "Rockhide boars. Skin like a scree slope, and it wears like one. Pilgrims' boots, mule harness, a Sandthrone jerkin if one comes asking." She grins. "Five hides. The boars wallow on the south slope, past the pines."
quests.complete: She bends a hide double; it barely creases. "That'll outlast us both."

steps.text: Take rockhides from the boars in the southern wallow.

quests.title: The Waystation Keeper
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Search the ruined waystation on the lower road for its last keeper's journal.
quests.offer:
"Before the Sandthrone came there was a waystation on the lower road. Grenna Holt kept it. The toll-guards burned it the week they took the gate, and nobody ever found her."

"She kept a journal, like I keep my book. It'll be in the hearth if it's anywhere; she hid everything in the hearth. Bring it back. Someone should know how it ended."
quests.complete: Maddoc reads the last page twice, then closes the journal. "She got the pilgrims out by the goat path. That's like her." He sets it on the shelf beside his own book.

steps.text: Search the ruined waystation on the lower road.

objectives.say: Behind a loose hearthstone, wrapped in oilcloth: a soot-black journal. The last pages are written fast.

steps.text: Bring Grenna's journal to Maddoc Vire.

quests.title: The Dead-Drop
quests.canonStatus: CANON factions (Sandthrone, Salt-Menders), GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Hadrik Sull will pay well for the Salt-Menders' letters hidden in a waymarker on the eastern descent. Taking this contract costs you standing with the Salt-Menders.
quests.offer:
The broker doesn't get up. "Everyone who comes up this road ends up killing a few of my Company's people. I don't hold it against them. It's trade. Everything is."

"Here's another. The Salt-Menders run people over this pass under our noses, and they leave letters for each other in a hollow waymarker on the east road down. I want those letters. Bring them, and the Company forgets a few of its dead, and you walk away with more coin than the pilgrims will ever pay you."

"The Menders won't thank you. But then, they never pay."
quests.complete: Hadrik counts coin onto the bench, more than you've seen in one place since Oakhaven. "The Company remembers who it trades with. So do the Menders, I'm told. Choose your friends."

steps.text: Take the Salt-Menders' letters from the hollow waymarker on the eastern descent.
Bring the letters to Hadrik Sull.

objectives.text: Sell the letters to Hadrik Sull
objectives.say: "Ciphered in salt-marks. Of course." He smiles and pockets them. "We have people who read salt."

quests.title: What the Pale Ones Watch
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Pale Things as cosmic watchers are canon (world_bible.md); the watchers on the high ledge are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Drive the Pale watchers off the high ledge above the east road, so Tarsk can see what they were watching.
quests.offer:
"Pale ones on the high ledge, above the east road. Three. They came when the escort went through, and they haven't moved since." Tarsk's voice is flat. "My people don't fight the Pale. We don't know that they can be fought. But you have a way of making things stop being where they stand."

"Make them stop. Then I'll go up and look at what they were looking at."
quests.complete: Tarsk comes down from the ledge an hour later and says nothing for a long time. "They were watching the road to Argentis," he says at last. "Not the road. What's at the end of it."

steps.text: Drive the Pale watchers off the high ledge.

quests.title: What the Mine Gave Back
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (Hollow Men) and tunnels (book2 ch.19); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Hollow Men are walking out of the old mine west of the Rest. Look at the Sealed Adit, then put them down.
quests.offer: Maddoc keeps his book shut on his knee. "The old adit, west along the ore road. The Company bricked it up the year they took the gate. Said the tunnels ran too far east, under the grey." He looks at the window, not at you. "Something's come out of it anyway. Grey things, walking slow. Go and look at the bricks first. Then do what has to be done."
quests.complete: "Five." Maddoc opens the book and writes nothing in it. "They were miners once, likely. Somebody's sons." He closes it. "Don't tell me what the bricks looked like. I've an idea."

steps.text: Look at the Sealed Adit, at the end of the ore road.

objectives.say: The bricks across the adit are Company work, and the mortar is new. Near the bottom it has been scratched away in long grooves, from the inside, by something with more patience than strength.

steps.text: Put down the Hollow Men out of the adit.

quests.title: Shadows on the Cold Tarn
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Pale Things); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Pale shadows stand in the shallows of the Cold Tarn, north under the wall. Tarsk wants them gone.
quests.offer: Tarsk is sharpening nothing; the blade is already sharp. "The tarn. North, under the wall. Three shadows stand in the shallows at dusk, looking down." He tests the edge on his thumb. "The pale ones on the ledge look at the road. These look at the water. I don't know what's in the water. I'd rather they stopped."
quests.complete: Tarsk nods once. "Good." A long pause. "Did you look? In the water?" He doesn't wait for an answer. "No. Better not."

steps.text: Clear the pale shadows from the Cold Tarn.

objectives.say: The last shadow comes apart like breath on a cold morning, and the tarn is only water again.

quests.title: Grey Robes on the East Road
quests.canonStatus: CANON factions (Sandthrone, Salt-Menders), GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Men in pilgrims' grey are stopping carts at the Broken Post on the eastern descent. Hadrik wants them dead and their packs searched.
quests.offer: Hadrik turns a coin over his knuckles. "Pilgrims at the Broken Post. Grey robes, cairn-stones, very holy." The coin stops. "Pilgrims don't stop carts. These do, and the carts they stop are carts my gate let through. Somebody is selling the gate's tally. Kill the pilgrims, open their packs, and bring me the name of whoever is doing the selling. Same terms as before."
quests.complete: Hadrik reads the list twice, then folds it very small. "A Sandthrone hand. One of mine." He pays you without counting. "The Company is grateful. The Company is also going to be busy for a few days."

steps.text: Kill the false pilgrims at the Broken Post.
steps.say: Under the grey robes, Company mail.

steps.text: Search the false pilgrims' packs.

objectives.say: Cairn-stones for show, Company knives for use, and folded small in a boot a list of every cart the gate let through this month, in a Sandthrone hand.

quests.title: What the Shrine Hears
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Silent Pilgrims are CANON; this shrine is not theirs by any book)
quests.summary: Maddoc wants someone to stand at the Listening Shrine after dark and tell Tarsk what it says.
quests.offer: "There's a shrine up on the north spur. No idol in it. Just an ear, cut in the stone." Maddoc rubs his own ear without noticing. "The pilgrims used to stand there at night and listen. They'd come down quiet. Go up after dark and listen. Then tell Tarsk, not me. He'll know what it means. I'm too old to want to."
quests.complete: Tarsk listens without moving. "Numbers. The gate's numbers." He spits to one side. "The stone has been counting what goes through the pass. Or something is counting, and using the stone to say it." He looks east. "The pale ones count too."

steps.text: Stand at the Listening Shrine after dark.

objectives.text: Listen at the shrine at night
objectives.say: The wind goes through the cut ear in the stone and comes out as a voice, very low, saying numbers: carts and mules and heads, one by one, the toll-gate's tally read back to the dark.

steps.text: Tell Tarsk what the shrine said.

quests.title: The Thing Under the Umbra Scarp
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (a Pale Thing); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: One pale shape stands under the Umbra scarp west of the Rest, counting whoever passes. Yara's drovers won't go near it.
quests.offer: Yara is tallying her own stock and keeps losing count. "There's a thing under the Umbra scarp, west. Pale. It stands and it watches the goat path, and my drovers say it counts them as they go by. Out loud." She puts the slate down. "Three of them have quit. I can't buy what doesn't come up the path. Make it stop counting."
quests.complete: "It's gone?" Yara picks the slate back up. "Then they'll come back. Drovers always come back, for money." She marks something. "I'll not ask what it was. You'll not tell me. That's a fair trade."

steps.text: Kill the Umbra Watcher under the Umbra scarp.

objectives.say: It stops counting halfway through a number, and the scarp is very quiet.

quests.title: Bears in the High Pines
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Mountain bears have come down into the high pines below the Cold Tarn, and they have taken two of the pilgrims' mules. Yara wants three of them dead.
quests.offer:
Yara Quell is mending a mule's harness that something has bitten clean through. "Bears. Grey ones, mountain bears, down in the high pines under the tarn." She holds up the harness. "Two mules this week. They don't come below the snow in a good year, and this isn't one."

"Three of them. Keep your back to a tree, and don't run: they're quicker than you downhill."
quests.complete: "Three." Yara turns a grey pelt over in her hands, thick as a blanket. "That's a winter's warmth for somebody up here." She folds it. "The mules will thank you. In their way."

steps.text: Kill the mountain bears in the high pines.

quests.title: Smoke on the Khaven Road
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: goblins (the Weavers of the Warrens) are CANON (world_bible.md) and the Sandthrone toll in the Peaks is CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md); Pib's kin, the pickets' signal and their hiding place are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Two of Pib's people are hiding in the pines below the Signal Tower, waiting for a chance to run for Khaven. Put down the pickets who watch the road, then whistle the goblins the all-clear.
quests.offer:
Pib has a lump of charcoal and is drawing on the back of a flour sack: a tower, a fire, a road going down. "The tower on the spur, over the Khaven road. Whenever anyone comes up it, the pickets throw green wood on their fire, and the gate sees the smoke before it sees you." He draws a great deal of smoke.

"When one of us gets out, we run that way, for Khaven. The smoke goes up and the riders come down." Two tiny marks go in among the pines under the tower. "Nim and Tobble. Three nights up a tree, waiting for a gap. Put the pickets down, then go to the edge of those pines and whistle. One note, held long. A tune means Company. The Company always whistles tunes."
quests.complete: Pib hears it all with his whole face. "Nim's the small one. She'll have glared at you. She glares at everyone she likes." He rubs the smoke off his sack with a thumb. "Khaven by morning, and then wherever goblins go." A pause. "Thank you. We don't say it often. It catches in the teeth."

steps.text: Put down the Sandthrone pickets at the Signal Tower, on the spur above the Khaven road.

objectives.say: The last picket goes down beside his own fire, and nobody throws on the green wood.

steps.text: Go to the edge of the pines below the Signal Tower and whistle one long note.

objectives.text: Whistle at the edge of the tower pines
objectives.say: You whistle one long note. For a while, nothing. Then two small grey shapes drop out of a pine, look at you very hard, and are away down the slope toward the Khaven road without a sound.

steps.text: Tell Pib his people are away.

quests.title: Stone Remembers
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Hollow Men are CANON (book1 ch.4); the goblins as the High City's old record-keepers and aether-geodes as fossilized memory are CANON (world_bible.md); that Pib can hear names in the hollows' grey stone is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Pib says stone remembers, and the grey stone off the Hollow Men by the Sealed Adit remembers best. Bring him five petrified shards from them.
quests.offer:
"Those grey walkers by the old adit." Pib doesn't look west when he says it. "The old man with the book thinks they were miners. They were. I can hear it on them when the wind's that way."

"Goblins kept the High City's records once, before the Purge. Every name, every light. You learn things, doing that, and the first thing you learn is that stone remembers. It's why the Company cuts the singing stones out of this mountain." He holds out his cupped hands. "Bring me the grey off the walkers when you put them down. Five pieces. If I hold each one to the right note I can hear who it was. Somebody ought to."
quests.complete:
Pib lays the five shards in a row on the bench and puts his ear to each in turn, humming under his breath, a different note for each. At the fourth he stops humming for a long time.

Then he finds a stub of pencil and writes, slowly, in big careful letters, like someone working in a hand that isn't his. "Five of them, in four stones. Two were brothers; they went into the one stone together." He folds the paper round a chip of the grey. "The fifth stone had forgotten already. I listened a long time."

steps.text: Bring Pib five petrified shards from the Hollow Men by the Sealed Adit, along the ore road west of the Rest.

objectives.say: "Gently. They were somebody." Pib takes them one at a time, the way you would take eggs from under a hen.

quests.title: Names for the Book
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Hollow Men (book1 ch.4) and the old mining tunnels under the Peaks (book2 ch.19) are CANON; the miners' names, Pib's list and the reading at the adit are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Read the names Pib heard in the grey stone aloud at the mouth of the Sealed Adit, then take his list to Maddoc Vire for his book.
quests.offer:
Pib pushes the folded paper across to you with one finger, as if it might be hot. "Two things want doing with this, and I can't do either of them."

"The names want saying where they were lost: at the mouth of the old adit, out loud, by a mouth that isn't a goblin's. The stone's more used to yours." His ears go flat. "Then take it to the old man with the book. He writes down everyone who goes up the road. These went up, and nobody wrote them down."
quests.complete:
Maddoc reads the list twice. Then he opens his book at a clean page and copies each name out in his best hand, with the day beside it, and on the last line he writes: one more, not known.

"Pell I knew," he says, without looking up. "Owed me for a loaf." He blots the page and closes the book on it. "I'll call that paid."

steps.text: Read the names aloud at the mouth of the Sealed Adit, at the end of the ore road.

objectives.text: Read the names at the Sealed Adit
objectives.say: You read them to the bricked mouth of the adit, one at a time: Pell. Oswy Dunn. Gil Mabe and Garret Mabe. Wat Corley. The wind drops while you read. When you have finished it gets up again, and somewhere behind the bricks a little grit runs down, and stops.

steps.text: Take Pib's list to Maddoc Vire at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.say: "What's this, then?" Maddoc unfolds the paper, and the chip of grey drops into his palm. He closes his hand on it and doesn't open it again.

quests.title: The Goatherd's Fold
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Wolves have moved into the pines by the old goatherd's fold, at the shieling on the drove track. Clear them out and look the fold over, so Maddoc can tell the goatherd it is still standing.
quests.offer:
Maddoc turns his book back a long way. "Wenlow Brack. Goatherd. Kept the shieling at the end of the drove track for forty years, and paid the toll in goats, two at a time, till there weren't any." He finds the line. "He's the only man I ever wrote in going down. He asked me to mind the fold till he came back."

"I can't mind it from here, and the wolves have moved in: a pack in the pines past the fold. Clear them out, and look the fold over for me, so I can tell him it's standing. If he asks."
quests.complete: "Standing, then." Maddoc writes something small in the margin by Wenlow's name. "Forty-one notches. That'll be the goats." He shuts the book. "If he ever comes back up the road he'll count them himself, and they'll be right. He never lost count of a goat in his life. Only of the years."

steps.text: Clear the wolves out of the pines by the Goatherd's Shieling, at the end of the drove track.
Look the old fold over at the shieling.

objectives.say: The fold walls are sound, if low. On the gatepost someone has cut a notch for every goat the toll took, forty-one of them, the last few cut deep. A bell hangs from a nail, its clapper tied up with twine so the wind can't ring it.

quests.title: No Deer on the Ash
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Ash-Walkers and their enclave in the caves of the Eastern Ridge are CANON (book1 ch.20); the custom of carrying hides home over the pass is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Nothing lives on the Ash Rim that you could make a boot from. Tarsk wants four hill-deer hides to carry home to the enclave.
quests.offer:
Tarsk is mending his boot with a strip cut from an older, worse boot. "On the ash there are no deer. There are crows, and what the crows eat." He pulls the stitch tight with his teeth. "Every Ash-Walker who comes over the pass carries hides home. That is the custom. I have been here a season and I have carried nothing."

"Hill deer graze in the east pines, in the high pines where the bears are, and by the tarn. They see you long before you see them. Go low, and go slow. Four hides."
quests.complete: Tarsk runs a thumb along each hide, checking the grain the way Yara checks coin. "Good. Boots for the children before the cold." He rolls them tight and binds them with salt-cord. "On the Rim they will ask where I got them. I will tell them: from someone who goes low and slow." It may be a joke. With Tarsk you can never be sure.

steps.text: Hunt the hill deer in the Peaks' pines and bring Tarsk four hides.

objectives.say: "Four." He counts them again anyway.

quests.title: Clipped Coin
quests.canonStatus: CANON faction (Sandthrone), GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Someone in the Company is clipping the toll coin before it reaches the strongbox. Hadrik Sull will pay for six clipped Sandthrone coins off the pickets and the gate-guards, as proof.
quests.offer:
Hadrik holds a coin up to the light between finger and thumb. "Desert gold. Struck in the south, honest weight. Now look at the edge." It has been pared like a fingernail. "Every coin that comes off this gate is a little lighter than the one that went into it. A shaving, no more. Fifty men and a shaving each, and somebody is buying himself a farm."

"The Company can't be seen taking coin off its own pickets. You, on the other hand, take it off them most days." He flicks you the coin. "Six more like that, off the pickets at the tower or the guards at the gate. Same terms as ever."
quests.complete:
Hadrik weighs each coin on the flat of his hand with his eyes shut, and names a figure for each. "A grain short. A grain. Two grains. A grain..." He opens his eyes and smiles without any pleasure in it. "The tower's coins are the lightest. They'll be skimming at the fire, where the watch can reach without getting up."

He pays you in coin that has not been clipped. You check.

steps.text: Take six clipped toll coins off the Sandthrone pickets at the Signal Tower or the guards at the toll gate, and bring them to Hadrik Sull.

objectives.say: "Let's see who's been at the shears." He spreads them on his knee.

quests.title: Where the Mountain Came Down
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the void slowly eating the Peaks' stone is CANON (world_bible.md) and so are the Salt-Menders; the grey at the avalanche scar and what it does to the boars are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The rockhides off the avalanche scar come back grey at the tips. Lisle Tamber wants five bristles from the boars that root there, to learn whether the grey takes living things.
quests.offer:
Lisle has one of Yara's rockhides spread over her knees and is going over it a hand's breadth at a time. "Yara says this one came off the avalanche scar, east, up the scree path past the switchback. Feel along the spine." The bristles there are grey at the tips, and smooth, and cold. "That isn't age. That's the scar."

"At the head of the scar the rock has gone grey, like the stone down the old adit. If it's getting into the boars that root by it, then it takes living things, and if it takes living things it can walk." She folds the hide. "Five bristles off the scar boars. Pull them, don't cut them; I want the roots. And wash your hands after."
quests.complete:
Lisle lays the bristles out on salt and watches them a long while. The grey creeps no further up the shafts, and down at the roots, where the boar was warm, there is none at all.

"It's on them, not in them." She sits back. "They rub against the grey and carry it about like wallow-mud. It doesn't take what's living." She writes that down, then adds two more words and underlines them twice: not yet.

steps.text: Pull grey-tipped bristles from the rockhide boars on the avalanche scar, up the scree path from the toll road.

objectives.say: Five bristles, each grey at the tip and cold, and each with its root.

steps.text: Bring the bristles to Lisle Tamber at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.say: "In here. Don't shake them." She holds out a fold of salted paper.

quests.title: Old Scree-Tusk
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the void slowly eating the Peaks' stone is CANON (world_bible.md); Old Scree-Tusk and the grey that has gone into him are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Old Scree-Tusk has rooted at the grey head of the avalanche scar for years. Look at where he roots, bring him down, and bring Lisle Tamber his hide, to learn why the grey has gone into him and not the others.
quests.offer:
"Not yet," Lisle says, tapping the words she underlined. "I don't like a finding with not yet in it."

"Yara's drovers talk about an old boar at the very head of the scar. Old Scree-Tusk. Bigger than a mule, they say, and he never leaves the grey. Roots in it, sleeps in it." She turns her pen over and over. "The others brush past it. He's stood in it for years. If the grey takes anything living, it'll have taken him. Go and look at where he roots, then bring him down and bring me his hide. Carry it on a stick, if you've any sense."
quests.complete:
The hide is grey right through, smooth as river stone, and it weighs next to nothing. Lisle doesn't lay salt on this one. She looks at it a long time without touching it.

"It takes what keeps still," she says at last. "Long enough in one place, and the grey stops telling you apart from the stone." She wraps the hide in salted cloth and ties it twice. "Remind me never to settle down."

steps.text: Look at the grey head of the avalanche scar, where Old Scree-Tusk roots, and bring him down for his hide.

objectives.text: Look at the head of the scar
objectives.say: The rock at the scar's head isn't broken; it's gone, smooth and grey, like wax that never warmed. Worn into it is a trench, boar-wide and knee-deep, where something has rooted in the same place for years. The bottom of the trench is grey too.
Old Scree-Tusk comes down the way the mountainside did, all at once and with a great deal of noise, and then the scar is quiet.
His hide comes away grey right through, smooth and cold, and so light the wind tries to take it.

steps.text: Bring Old Scree-Tusk's hide to Lisle Tamber at the Pilgrims' Rest.

objectives.say: "On the salt. Gently." She takes it off the stick, not out of your hands.

quests.title: Where the Song Thins
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and the Original Song are CANON (world_bible.md), and so is the void eating the Peaks' stone; the listening places and what is heard at them are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Brother Cael wants to know where the old song can still be heard in the pass and where it has gone thin. Listen at the Cold Tarn after dark, at the foot of the Umbra scarp and at the Broken Post on the east road.
quests.offer:
Brother Cael writes on his slate and turns it to you.

The pass used to sing all through. The old song, the first one, that the world was made to. Now there are places where it is thin.

He wipes the slate with his sleeve and writes again, smaller. I cannot leave the ear in the stone; it must be kept. Go where I tell you and listen. Not with your ears. Stand still until the wind stops being wind. The tarn's north shore, after dark. The foot of the Umbra scarp. The Broken Post on the east road.
quests.complete:
Cael hears your account with his brass tube held against his chest, as if to hear it twice. When you come to the Broken Post he stops you with a raised hand, and for a while he doesn't write anything.

Then he writes for a long time, copies it out fair on a clean page and gives it to you. The last line he has underlined: It is coming from the east. We knew. Now it is written.

steps.text: Listen at the three places Brother Cael named: the Cold Tarn's north shore after dark, the foot of the Umbra scarp, and the Broken Post on the east road.

objectives.text: The tarn's north shore, after dark
objectives.say: You stand still until the wind stops being wind. Under it, very faint, the tarn is ringing: one clear note, like a glass struck once and left to sound.

objectives.text: The foot of the Umbra scarp
objectives.say: Under the scarp the note is so low you feel it in your teeth before you hear it: the mountain's own, slow as breathing, and very old.

objectives.text: The Broken Post on the east road
objectives.say: At the Post the wind comes up out of the east, and it carries nothing at all. No note. Not even the sound of itself. You find you have been holding your breath, and you let it go.

quests.title: An Hour Without Eyes
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and the Archive of Silence are CANON (world_bible.md), the Sandthrone are a CANON company and their toll in the Peaks is CANON-EXPANDED (the draft chapter_5.md); the six pilgrims and their crossing are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Six Silent Pilgrims are waiting in the pines below the toll gate to carry Brother Cael's notes south to the Archive, and the Sandthrone captain holds every pilgrim he sees from his eyrie. Make sure he sees nothing, and watch them through from the eyrie.
quests.offer:
Brother Cael has a folded page sewn into a linen cover, and his slate is already written on when you come.

Six of my order wait in the pines below the gate, to go over and carry this south to the Archive. From his eyrie the captain sees every pilgrim on the road, and every pilgrim he sees he holds at the gate until the toll is paid. We have nothing to pay with. We never have.

He wipes the slate and writes one more line: The captain must see nothing for an hour.

He does not write how. He looks at your weapon, and then, with great care, at the sky.
quests.complete:
Cael hears you out with his eyes shut. When you tell him the six went through the gate without a word said, he writes one line and holds it up a long time, so you are sure to read it.

Thank you.

Then he rubs it out, slowly, and writes it again, as if once were not enough.

steps.text: Bring down the Sandthrone captain in his eyrie above the toll gate.

objectives.say: The captain goes down on his own lookout, and for the first time in a long while nobody is watching the road.

steps.text: Watch the gate from the captain's eyrie while the pilgrims go through.

objectives.text: Watch the gate from the eyrie
objectives.say: Below, a file of masked pilgrims in dyed linen comes out of the gate pines and up to the gate. With no word from the eyrie the guards fall to arguing over whose job it is to stop them, and while they argue the pilgrims walk through, one after another, and are gone round the bend of the road.
